launches.tagline: The customer service agency for B2C companies. Your entire customer support operation, one line on your expense sheet.
launches.body:
![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=98342&key=user_uploads/72181/7afbff3c-0ba0-4254-8473-0810886e91fa)

Hi everyone, we’re [Marie](https://www.linkedin.com/in/marie-schneegans/) and [Michae](https://www.linkedin.com/in/michaelfester/)l, and we’re building [14.ai](http://14.ai): the AI-native customer service agency. Our customers include AI glasses company Brilliant, men’s health supplement company Sperm Worms, Nordic lighting company Creative Lighting, and luxury skincare brand Yon-Ka. Michael previously co-founded Snips, an AI voice platform acquired by Sonos.

**The problem: the death loop of customer service**

We’ve all been there: you have a simple problem that you take to customer support, but you’re forced into a never-ending cycle of being passed between different agents and explaining your situation for the (n + 1)th time.

**1. The burden of effort:** If a customer is working harder than the company to solve a problem, the system has failed.

**2. Fragmentation:** You start a chat on your phone, move to your desktop, and have to explain your account number and issue for the third time.

**3. Dumb automation:** You talk with a chatbot that acts as a gatekeeper, not a helper.

**4. Costly, slow onboarding:** Onboarding a new customer support agent brings an expensive and time-consuming burden.

Traditional BPOs (Business Process Outsourcing) try to solve this through headcount in low-cost regions, and rely on manual processes and legacy CRMs that are slow to adapt and prone to error. This approach does not work.

### **The solution: [14.ai](http://14.ai) is the AI-native customer service agency**

We are a full-service agency built from the ground up with AI as the core engine.

#### **1. High-touch concierge**

Excellent service guides everything we do. After our customers hand over their existing integrations, we tell them to stop answering tickets; now, it’s our problem. This level of service extends to our customer’s customers. We offer the best customer service in the world, and we are always working to stay that way.

#### **2. Low constant onboarding**

[14.ai](http://14.ai) goes live within hours. We take away the burden of onboarding new customer support agents and begin answering your tickets immediately. We get our customers to inbox zero on day zero.

#### **3. Agentic resolution**

Most bots just provide “how-to” links. [14.ai](http://14.ai) actually does the work. We plug in to your company’s most complex processes, autonomously verifying purchases, generating shipping labels, and triggering refunds in a single, seamless flow.

#### **4. Outcomes, not tools**

Our AI engineers operate our own highly tailored software for automation. Customers only see the parts they actually need to see: reports, CX metrics, resolved conversations, VIP or high-touch integrations, and the like.

#### **5. The human-AI feedback loop**

Our human team is supercharged, not replaced. We also service our customers around the clock, 24/7.

Our full-time AI engineers are based in San Francisco and are responsible for answering every support ticket, automated or not. Every time we encounter an edge case, that intervention is fed back into our agents - they become smarter every day.

### **Who is this for?**

**E-commerce companies, mobile applications, fintech companies, healthcare companies, and more.** These are types of companies we’ve worked with already and have seen huge impact with. Customer relationships begin with a 7-day free trial, allowing for onboarding and for potential customers to confirm that there is a fit.

Every customer we have onboarded repurposed their support teams before their trial even finished.

We thrive where volume is high and customer support is managed by a number of human customer support agents, either domestically or overseas. If you’re a company with a backlog of support tickets, even better: we’ll take care of your entire backlog on Day 1.

### **Our ask**

We want to be your customer service. If you’re tired of managing a fragmented support team, fighting with legacy BPOs and VAs, or having a backlog of support tickets, we’d love to talk.

**Visit our website at[ ](https://14.ai)[14.ai](http://14.ai) or book an intro call with us here.**

### **Also! We’re launching the world’s first autonomous consumer brand: GloGlo**

[GloGlo](https://gloglo.com/) are rapid glucose gummies designed for Type 1 diabetics, high-performance athletes, and more. They are built to deliver rapid and reliable carbohydrates, meeting quality-of-life pain points that glucose tablets don’t address and elevating the consumption experience from existing options. The brand is powered by [14.ai](http://14.ai), meaning we are owning and operating GloGlo from the ground up. GloGlo is a blueprint for how B2C companies can operate at a world-class level autonomously, while delivering the best possible customer experience. Check it out at [gloglo.com](http://gloglo.com).

launches.tagline: Close customer support tickets faster with AI
launches.body:
Hi YC!

We’re [Marie](https://twitter.com/marieschneegans) and [Michael](https://twitter.com/michaelfester) from [Markprompt.](https://markprompt.com)

We are building AI infrastructure to power customer support at scale. We are live with companies like AngelList, Mindbody, and Plotly.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=76470&key=user_uploads/72181/65f672d8-ad2b-4f01-843a-75653e4010ab)

**Problem**

* **Scaling customer support with headcount is expensive:** Human resources account for 90%+ of customer support expenses.
* **Customer support agents burn out:** Support tasks incur large amounts of manual, repetitive, and ungratifying work that humans don't need to be doing, causing burnout, turnover, and reduced quality.
* **Customer support is more than a chatbot on a website:** In an API-driven world, customer support tools need to evolve with the company’s tech stack. Existing AI-powered solutions are not delivering on the promise, resulting in sub-par customer experience and low NPS and CSAT scores.
* **Company resources are siloed across systems:** As companies grow, so does their expert knowledge. It is hard to access at scale, and keeping employees up-to-date is nearly impossible.

**Solution**

* **Comprehensive data indexing:** Markprompt addresses the root of the information access problem by indexing all available knowledge within a company, setting the foundation for a robust system of record to feed the AI. This includes:
  * Salesforce Knowledge databases
  * Salesforce and Zendesk tickets
  * Notion wikis
  * GitHub repositories, discussions, and issues
  * Company websites, docs, guides, blogs
* **An API-first approach:** Markprompt is built from the ground up with an API-first approach. Every feature, from indexing and processing of data to generating drafts, triaging tickets, creating chat replies, or triggering automations, can be achieved via our APIs. Markprompt also provides SDKs (such as React hooks and components) and no-code tools to enable integrations at all touchpoints in the customer journey.
* **Deep integrations:** Markprompt works well within existing support platforms, such as Zendesk and Salesforce. And with our APIs, it is possible to build custom integrations to accommodate any setup.

Here is an example of a bespoke ticket deflection and triaging system built with our React libraries:

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=76470&key=user_uploads/72181/52faa2d8-f529-4ce4-8314-a3f6e5cba849)

**How we help**

* **Efficient ticket deflection:** Deploy AI-driven chatbots and ticket deflection systems that efficiently handle routine queries, allowing support teams to focus on more complex cases.
* **Accelerated case resolution:** Use automated drafts to streamline case resolution, ensuring faster response times based on the up-to-date expert knowledge.
* **Actionable AI agents:** Enable AI agents to perform user actions, such as processing refunds or canceling a subscription, with high accuracy.

**Who we are**

We are life partners, and passionate about design and AI. Michael previously founded Snips (acq. by Sonos), a privacy-respecting voice AI platform that now powers all voice interactions on Sonos speakers. Marie and Michael previously founded [Motif](https://motif.land), a collaborative docs platform based on Markdown and React. While building Motif, we realized that the tasks of maintaining company expert knowledge up to date and providing stellar customer support are intimately connected, and both can in large part be automated. This led us to build Markprompt.

We are backed by founders and operators at Algolia, Microsoft, Snowflake, Stripe and Vercel.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=76470&key=user_uploads/72181/19f7c2ed-c74f-4e4a-b959-454f7645b039)

**Our asks**

* **Introductions:** We're looking for tech-savvy companies processing 1000+ customer support tickets per month. Please let us know if you have connections to these companies, especially folks leading Eng or Customer Support. Please introduce us via [founders@markprompt.com](mailto:founders@markprompt.com).
* **Book a demo:** [here](https://calendly.com/markprompt/30min).

Hey everyone! We're [Guru](https://linkedin.com/in/gururao1) and [Michael](https://www.linkedin.com/in/michaelpnguyen/) from [DigitalCarbon](https://www.digitalcarbon.ai/).\
\
**Tl;dr**\
DigitalCarbon transforms images and videos into photorealistic, editable 3D scenes. Create virtual home tours or show off products in 3D using just your phone - no special gear needed!

[ ](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=c2Pw63zE94I)
\
**❌ The Problem: Creating 3D environments is complex and slow**

Billions of images and videos are captured daily, but turning them into immersive 3D experiences is challenging:

* Requires specialized, expensive equipment
* Rendering is painfully slow, limiting real-time applications

launches.body:
**tl;dr: Embedding these insurance products generates additional revenue, protects customers, and boosts customer loyalty at zero cost. And it’s as easy as signing up for Facebook if you still remember that!** 😉 — [**_Talk to us._**](https://meetings.hubspot.com/manishchauhan/discussion-booking-extended-hours)

_—_\
\
Hello, everyone! We are Manish and Sanket (right to left), the team behind SureBright. We started our professional journey together with our first job at Samsung Research Institute 14 years ago. \
\
[**Manish**](https://www.linkedin.com/in/manishchauhan01/) **(CEO)**, a graduate of the University of Waterloo (MMath, CS) and INSEAD (MBA), has developed products for industry giants like Amazon and serves on the board of the InsurTech Association. [**Sanket**](https://www.linkedin.com/in/sanketmunjal/) **(CTO)** has led engineering departments at insurtechs such as Policy Bazaar, which has become a household name in India. Together, we bring 25 years of combined experience in insurtechs, startups, major tech companies, and business.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=83656&key=user_uploads/456731/48122b44-2e46-4967-8d6f-81c645ca259d)

Warranty and insurance distribution in e-commerce has seen minimal change, with the industry evolving slowly. At Surebright, we're on a mission to revolutionize this by leveraging the latest advancements in generative AI. Our platform enables US and Canadian merchants to seamlessly integrate Apple Care-like warranty programs for any eligible product, from ovens to bikes. We achieve this with nearly zero onboarding and operating costs, allowing merchants to offer these warranties in just minutes across any sales channel.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=83656&key=user_uploads/456731/62878cfc-f33a-4731-82c6-022f2614970f)

### **What is the problem? ❌**

The cost of offering product warranties is exponentially high for merchants and insurers. As it follows,

1. **Resource-Intensive Integration:** Merchants must create a file transfer-based system to integrate with insurers. Additionally, they need to develop internal tools to apply the correct warranty plans to products, build custom UIs, and manage data collection, sharing, and tracking to meet both insurer and regulatory requirements. This entire process can take **six months to a year to go live**.
2. **Recurring Additional Work:** Maintaining integrations and tools requires dedicated engineering teams. Running the warranty program also requires dedicated time from the operation team. This usually requires **additional hiring**.

Below is what the current merchant landscape looks like,

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=83656&key=user_uploads/456731/0e70aa2b-9c2e-41d7-bc6d-6b292f383590)

### **How is SureBright Solving these problems? 🎉**

SureBright’s **warranty program runs on auto-pilot**, empowering merchants of all sizes and providing the following key benefits:

1. **99% less onboarding time, no onboarding or operating costs**, and no recurring tasks or hiring required. Our end-to-end automated solution ensures you never worry about the warranty program.
2. **Cover any product** under warranty and offer other insurance products, such as Shipping Insurance, without lifting a finger.
3. **Enjoy the highest warranty conversions** in the industry, averaging around 20.2%.

**With these benefits, we help merchants boost their bottom line** by up to 12% through warranty margin share. Offering warranties also increases customer trust in the brand, leading to 15.6% more conversions and a 14% increase in Average Order Value. In addition, customers get a better post-purchase experience, resulting in more repeat customers and fewer negative reviews.

### **The “aha” moment? 🎯🧠🧨**

We began our journey to help smaller merchants (<$100M in sales) offer warranties. But, within 3-4 months of going live, we began attracting interest from larger merchants. **The “aha” moment came when Insurance companies started utilizing our platform for their customers.** This was a pivotal moment, leading us to develop SureBright as the Stripe for embedded e-commerce insurance products.

Today, our customers include a diverse range of merchants and marketplaces with $0.5M to $1B in sales, insurance companies, tech firms involved in consumer product purchase journeys (such as Buy Now Pay Later), warranty management companies, and other insurtechs.

You can explore our consumer journey with partners such as [**Blackstone**](https://blackstoneproducts.com/products/blackstone-pizza-oven)**, **[**Magnum Bikes**](https://magnumbikes.com/products/magnum-pathfinder-t)**, **[**WalkingPad**](https://www.walkingpad.com/products/walkingpad-c2-foldable-walking-machine)**, and Street Cred Capital (BNPL).**

### **How can you help? 🙏**

If you know any merchant, marketplace, or company participating in the consumer purchase journey, such as Buy Now Pay Later and Checkout Management Companies, please make the introduction. We and they will both be very thankful! Email: [manish@surebright.com](mailto:manish@surebright.com) or [**_BOOK A CALL DIRECTLY WITH US._**](https://meetings.hubspot.com/manishchauhan/discussion-booking-extended-hours)

name: No Logo
long_description:
No Logo is building the orchestration layer for creating viral consumer products. The manufacturing world is full of capable, underutilized overseas factories with the machines, tooling, and engineers to build winning products – but no way to connect them to the creators and brands with the ideas and distribution. As a result, bringing a new product to market has traditionally taken 6-12 months, tens of thousands of dollars, and a team of 20-30 people.

No Logo collapses that. Using generative AI, we take a creator's product idea, visualize it, break it into core components and manufacturing processes, and match each step to the right factory in our network – turning an idea into a shippable product in just a few weeks.
one_liner: Turn ideas into physical products

launches.title: No Logo: Turn any idea into a real, manufactured product
launches.tagline: Building the orchestration layer for physical product creation
launches.body:
The last twenty years have made starting a business seamless. Shopify solved the store. Stripe solved payments. TikTok solved distribution. Manufacturing is the one piece that never moved. Launching a single new product still takes 6 to 12 months, tens of thousands of dollars upfront, and a team of specialists. Most great product ideas die before they become something you can hold.

We are building the orchestration layer for physical product creation, bridging the gap between customer demand and manufacturing supply.

It works like this. You describe an idea. Our AI visualizes it with you, breaks it into components and manufacturing processes, and matches each step to the right factory in our network. We run production, QC, and fulfillment, going from idea to a growing brand in about a month with no upfront costs.

We are not putting logos on mugs. We create entirely new consumer products: a digital camera that clips onto a purse, a lava-lamp humidifier, a painting that glows like the sun. We are starting with creators whose audiences have already validated demand; production happens only after demand exists, not before.

So far we’ve launched hundreds of products, shipped tens of thousands of items, and reached creator audiences totaling more than 90M people. Every product we create makes the network faster and smarter for the next one.

Have a product idea your audience keeps asking for? We'll make it real. [nologo.com](http://nologo.com)

**TLDR:** Anglera is the foundational AI layer that transforms messy product data into structured, searchable, enriched content at scale.

---

### **🔥 The Problem**

While everyone's building AI apps, there's a massive infrastructure gap underneath: **product data is broken at scale.**

* **Poor Discoverability** - 20% of searches return zero results due to missing/inconsistent information
* **Low Conversion** - Data errors cause 23% loss in impressions and 14% drop in conversions
* **Slow Time-to-Market -** Weeks of delays getting new products live due to manual data entry

**Result:** Billions in lost revenue from broken infrastructure.

The tech stack looks like this today:

```
Beautiful frontend shopping UI/UX
↓
Intelligent search & discovery algorithms
↓
Messy, unstructured product data ← ✨ We fix this
```

We've built AI agents that automatically transform any product data source into clean, structured, enriched content:

* **Input:** Messy spreadsheets, PDFs, images, brand websites, supplier feeds 
* **Output**: Complete, enriched product catalogs, continuously optimized for AI discoverability
* **Scale:** Process thousands of SKUs in seconds, not weeks.

long_description:
Riveter fully automates web data extraction, end to end. With a single API, agents can search, scrape, and structure data from the web. 

Customers like Snapchat and OpenAI use us to enrich datasets using Riveter's AI search agents that combine data from the web with third party or internal data.  

Their AI agents, custom scrapers, and integrations pack the power of browser use and automation for search, at a cost that allows for scale. 

You can even create a custom data API for repeated searches live in your app or internal databases. 

Perplexity and ChatGPT are great for single questions, but they can’t handle large amounts of data at once. And they’re working with a single agent and context window instead of one in every cell.

And Riveter’s web browsing can go further—even reading PDFs and images that may contain answers. 

Most teams still spend hours (or hire UpWorkers/contractors) to manually copy product specs, check competitor pricing, pull custom KYB/KYC data to assess customer risk, or scrape filings. Or they spend months building web scrapers, and when that still doesn't work, they come to Riveter.

Our founding team (Cody Watters - CTO, Abby Grills, CEO) brings deep product and engineering expertise from to YC-backed companies Gusto, Retool, and Middesk.

**❌ The Problem**

Almost any list you could ever need can be derived from the web. Every law firm in California. Every vet practice by state. Every competitor's pricing page. The information is out there.

The problem is getting it out.

Current options all hit the same wall:

* **Data vendors** sell you records from a static index -- outdated the moment you buy them, and missing anything outside their database

Riveter agents navigate the web the way a researcher would -- running searches, visiting pages, reading results -- and return a fully structured, enriched dataset.

launches.title: 🚀 Riveter API: Replace your entire scraper infrastructure with a single API
launches.tagline: Power your product with real data from the web.
launches.body:
We’re excited to launch our most requested feature: the **Riveter API**.

Web data is one of the biggest unlocks for what’s now possible with AI. But retrieving and structuring that data for your product or agents is far more complicated than it should be.

---

### **The Problem**

You need data from the web to equip your agents with more information or pipe structured data directly into your product.

But when it comes to web scraping, the gap between _idea_ and _working solution_ is huge.

* What starts as **“just a simple scraper” often turns into a patchwork of 5+ vendors** (SERP providers, proxy networks, headless browsers, scraper libraries, and infrastructure) leading to weeks or months of engineering effort.
* Timelines creep, **engineering costs rise, and maintaining scrapers becomes an ongoing burden**. All of this distracts your team from building your _core product._

https://youtu.be/1pFXQJExRGw

---

### **The Solution**

**Riveter** is the all-in-one web search agent. Configuration is simple — your team defines what data they need, and Riveter handles everything else.

* **Prompt-based configuration, tool selection, and custom formatting.** Tell Riveter what you need via a prompt, then select tools like web search, scraper, PDF reader, or image reader.
* **Everything built in.** SERP/search, proprietary scrapers, proxy management, and browser infrastructure are fully integrated, so you don’t have to build or connect multiple systems.
* **Structured, consistent output.** Apply custom tags or enums, specify date formats, or define JSON objects to get clean, predictable results every time.

The API routes data directly into your app — giving you real, grounded web data with minimal engineering overhead.

### **How It Works**

You can either **create a project in Riveter** to reference in your API request, or **configure all input and output fields directly in the API call.**

#### **Option 1: Creating an API request from a Riveter project**

Creating a project allows you to test and refine prompts and formatting before fetching data via the API.

**Best for:**

* Running recurring or long-term data collection
* Quickly testing and iterating on prompts and tools
* Structuring data that needs to be ingested by code

#### **Option 2: Configuring input/output fields directly in the API request**

On-the-fly configuration gives you the flexibility to change columns and prompts dynamically based on your inputs.

**Best for:**

* Giving AI agents access to create their own Riveter requests
* Handling variable outputs - e.g., running an initial request with Riveter, then defining attributes to evaluate your product or dataset on

### **Getting Started**

We can’t wait to see what you build with Riveter!

Head to[ ](https://riveterhq.com?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[**riveterhq.com**](http://riveterhq.com) and click **Get Started** — your first 500 searches are free!

Need a hand?[ Grab time here](https://riveterhq.com/contact?utm_source=chatgpt.com) and we’ll help you get set up.

We're [Evandro](https://www.linkedin.com/in/evandronadal), [Jack](https://www.linkedin.com/in/johnpconsidine/), and [Mike,](https://github.com/consofine) and we're building Getcho, a local retail delivery platform for high-value products. Getcho runs on top of third-party fleets, delivering $250,000 of merchandise per month.

## The problem

Merchants have embraced local / on-demand delivery—it boosts sales with urgent shoppers and is cheap, thanks to mega-fleets like DoorDash, Roadie, and Uber. But locally delivered packages are lost, misdelivered, or returned up to 10% of the time; some retail locations spend thousands of dollars each day replacing lost packages.

## The solution

Getcho prevents 95% of failed local deliveries. This saves merchants the costs associated with shipping replacements and, just as important, improves customers' perception of the merchant's brand.

By flagging GPS irregularities, using AI-assisted calls and texts to guide drivers at pick-up & drop-off, and scheduling around customer availability, Getcho ensures seamless and reliable deliveries.

## Demo

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GFxJq_xekfI>

## About us

Jack and Evandro ("Dro") met in college. They started a software development firm called K-Optional that they ran for seven years. Mike, Jack's brother, joined K-Optional in 2021.

There they built logistics products that were acquired or continue to generate millions in revenue, including:

* A [pig tracking](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pigging) platform that uses hardware and GPS data to check diagnostics on massive oil pipelines.
* A scheduling platform in the catastrophe insurance space that maps claimants to appraisal locations.

They spun Getcho out of a curbside pick-up application and went all in once they had delivered a million dollars of merchandise.

If you or someone you know is in retail operations, we'd love to connect & chat.

launches.body:
### **tl;dr**

We work with specialist clinics to identify their biggest administrative blockers and deploy custom **AI** to resolve them. Right now, we’re automating **referral intake**, reducing the time it takes for clinics to process new patients and accelerate revenue collection.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=u403AnLMSNE>

### **Problem**

Specialist clinics struggle with **slow, manual referral processing**, leading to revenue delays, administrative overload, and patient drop offs. The biggest bottlenecks we've uncovered:

* **Referral processing is manual and slow.** Clinics receive **thousands of referrals per month**, requiring extensive manual effort to extract and enter data.
* **Medical necessity verification is tedious.** Clinics must determine if a referral meets insurance criteria, often requiring **days of back-and-forth with primary care providers** for missing information.
* **Insurance approvals are a major roadblock.** Clinics waste **days negotiating with insurers** to confirm reimbursement eligibility before scheduling treatment.

These inefficiencies cause **40-60% of referrals to drop off and** costs the U.S. healthcare system **over $150 billion annually**. The administrative burden is also immense, with an average of **4.3 administrative staff per doctor** in the American healthcare system.

### **Solution**

![](https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXduwoVo9LiyuYd4ldqDHoJxHu2uaKzKbOzQnI4MZ0vlWDvKTY-nE2iokzaFTCR7-7PeqhwdI9FIqtRbpP1FkZ3ivWq6TdtuyftWnKoMCyzw-smhtrM7tZacSCTnDkJ45wF92PRK7w?key=9LANEIwzbMw6NQWGiMH6ii1e)

Cenote eliminates the **referral-to-treatment bottleneck**, allowing clinics to focus on patient care while accelerating revenue collection.

* **Automated data extraction:** We categorize and extract key referral details the moment they hit the clinic’s inbox.
* **Seamless medical necessity verification:** If critical referral data is missing, our system **auto-requests** the necessary information via the preferred form of digital communication.
* **AI-powered insurance authorization:** Our **AI callers** handle insurance approvals, freeing clinic staff to focus on higher-value tasks.

1. It's not about training the model. Everyone gets this wrong. When someone asks, the model runs a live search, reads what it finds, and picks. What decides it is boring and specific: a catalog structured so the model can trust it, and the right content on the sources it reads.
2. Existing tools were built for SaaS. They hand you a score and stop. That playbook breaks the moment you have 5,000 SKUs and variants. A brand and retailers unit of AEO is the catalog, not a homepage.

**The Solution:** Our solution is simple. First, we run a full audit of how you show up across AI search. Second, we build your roadmap. Lastly, we optimize your product catalog and create the content that gets you recommended. After 30 days, we tend to see a 5x increase in revenue.

**About Me:** Kaushik Mahorker (Founder & CEO). Previously, I was an Engineering Manager at Scale AI, where I led the GenAI Allocation team and built the ecommerce enrichment engine that structured 2.4M attributes across 400K SKUs, helping close $15M+ in retail and marketplace contracts.

name: Prox
long_description:
Prox turns product expertise into revenue for equipment manufacturers.

Equipment buyers rarely begin with a model number. They begin with a job, an installed system, a constraint, or a problem. The knowledge needed to qualify, recommend, configure, quote, repair, replace, or upgrade the product is scattered across manuals, catalogs, spreadsheets, calculators, product managers, applications engineers, dealer processes, support teams, and legacy systems. The result is abandoned demand, slow qualification, wrong-fit recommendations, quote delays, weak dealer follow-up, missed parts and service revenue, and dependence on a few experienced people.

Prox builds AI product specialists for equipment manufacturers. A product specialist uses the manufacturer's approved product knowledge, expert rules, calculators, and connected systems to move customers and frontline teams from a complex product question to the right purchase, quote, dealer, parts, service, replacement, or upgrade path.

How it works:

1. Understand what the person is trying to accomplish.
2. Resolve the product, application, and operating context already available.
3. Ask only for the missing information that changes the result.
4. Apply approved sources, expert rules, and deterministic tools (calculators, selectors, configurators, comparisons).
5. Produce a supported, cited recommendation, configuration, procedure, or decision artifact.
6. Move the person into the correct cart, quote, RFQ, BOM, dealer, sales, parts, service, replacement, upgrade, or expert action with the context preserved.

One product specialist, many governed skills: product discovery and comparison, sizing and configuration, competitive defense, quote preparation, dealer enablement, installation and commissioning, troubleshooting, parts identification, and approved service, replacement, and upgrade paths. Manufacturers deploy those skills to customers, dealers, sales teams, applications engineers, support teams, or field service. Existing CRM, CPQ, commerce, and support systems stay in place.

Support and service are revenue-bearing surfaces. The specialist resolves the customer's problem first, then surfaces the approved part, service, replacement, or upgrade path only when the evidence supports it.
one_liner: AI product specialists for equipment manufacturers

Greg and Dima here - childhood friends, grew up in our families’ warehouses - now YC founders building Prox.

**launch video:** https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9Ywl-K7ncj0

---

**tldr:**

[**Prox**](https://www.prox.inc/) builds digital workforce for third-party logistics and fulfillment providers. We deployed our first agents at [**ShipBob**](https://www.linkedin.com/company/shipbob) (unicorn 3PL handling 100+ million packages per year) to automate carrier claims for lost-in-transit packages. **They're now live in production, processing hundreds of claims in parallel and on track to recover millions in carrier refunds annually.**

**what is 3PL?**

third-party logistics companies (3PLs) are the invisible infrastructure behind e-commerce brands: they warehouse inventory, fulfill orders, manage returns, and negotiate with carriers so brands don't have to.

**the problem:**

40,000+ 3PLs in the US all do the same thing: throw people at operational bottlenecks.

❌ Claims processing done manually, one by one \
❌ Invoice reconciliation eating hours of labor \
❌ Compliance paperwork blocking growth \
❌ Every increase in package volume = more back-office hires

That's the margin trap. Logistics companies stuck at 3-5% margins because headcount scales linearly with volume of packages. You can't compound when labor costs are linear.

**what we built:**

We developed an n8n-inspired agent building platform - native to logistics infrastructure. It integrates with Salesforce, warehouse & transportation management systems, carrier portals, Microsoft Teams, and email → then executes SOPs end-to-end.

With this platform, we can deploy agents in production in a matter of days.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=95414&key=user_uploads/3066807/dc3e69b6-c3f6-476d-94c5-578b3a02d9de)

**use case: ShipBob Carrier Claims Automation**

Here’s an example of how our agents handle lost package claims for [ShipBob](https://shipbob.com/), one of the biggest 3PLs in the US.

> first demo at ShipBob HQ in Chicago
>
> ![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=95414&key=user_uploads/3066807/cd110709-17ec-410e-90c8-e3c0d7db72f5)


When a package goes missing - our agent orchestrates resolution: pull order data, calculates refund amounts, files with carriers, monitors responses, parses updates, syncs internal systems, escalates exceptions - hundreds running in parallel.

Our agents do not stop at task execution - we designed them to own outcomes. If a carrier doesn't respond, the agent follows up. If documentation is missing, it fetches it. Each agent has one objective: get the claim resolved.

**about us:**

[**Gregory Makodzeba:**](https://www.linkedin.com/in/gregory-makodzeba/)

* Founded Rektoff: built blockchain security infrastructure protecting $100B+ in crypto assets (clients: Solana Foundation)

* Grew up implementing ERP and WMS systems in the family distribution business

[**Dima Yanovsky:**](https://www.linkedin.com/in/yanovsk/)

* MIT grad: Computer Science + Electrical Engineering
* Robotics research at MIT CSAIL under Prof. Pulkit Agrawal on manipulation policies;
* Built internal and customer-facing AI agents at Pulley (YC W20) during early GPT era

We both grew up in our parents' warehouses. When we weren't moving boxes around, we were doing the mundane back-office work every warehouse has (filing claims, reconciling invoices, chasing carriers). This was the pre-LLM era, so we had no choice but to grind through manual workflows. We saw firsthand how coordination became the biggest constraint on growth - and how no software could actually handle it end-to-end.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=95414&key=user_uploads/3066807/68380300-ee0e-4379-98de-de1b551b269e)

We deeply understand the ontology of logistics operations. That's why we can ship integrations in days, not months. We're building the digital workforce we wish existed back then.

Hi! We’re [George](https://www.linkedin.com/in/george-lawrence-aab0011a6/) and [Alex](https://www.linkedin.com/in/alexanderschiff/), and we’re building [Channel3](https://trychannel3.com): **a database of every product on the internet.**

**What?**

Every time you shop on Google, Amazon, or ChatGPT, you’re querying a product database. These companies have built massive product catalogs — with pricing, availability, images, and specs — but they keep this data private. That means only the giants can build shopping experiences. Channel3 is changing that. We’re building a universal product catalog and giving every developer access.

**Got it. What can I use a product database for?**

Any website, app, or AI agent can boost revenue by adding commerce – without holding inventory or processing payments. You could, for example, build a kitchen co-pilot that suggests the best tools for every cook, or a fitness app that intelligently recommends equipment needed for the next class.

**How do I make money with Channel3?**

Monetization is built in. With Channel3, developers earn commission on every sale they drive — no chasing affiliate deals, no ads that break trust, and no subscription fees users won't pay.

**Why now?**

Multimodal models have only just become accurate and cheap enough to recognize products visually and semantically, letting us match duplicates across merchants, structure heaps of messy data, and link variants like color or size.

As AI models get smarter and cheaper, our flywheel accelerates: our catalog will improve, and it will be even easier for developers and vibe-coders to build on our infrastructure.

**Why we’re building this**

Alex discovered this problem firsthand while building an AI teacher that could recommend appropriate products for its students. He discovered that giving AI agents shopping capabilities is both a real pain-point and a growing opportunity, so he persuaded George, his smartest friend from Duke and former co-founder, to leave Palantir and build the solution together.

**I’m in! What now?**

We’re looking for developers who want to build the next generation of shopping on top of Channel3 (and get paid to do it!).

Valuable inventory sits unsold, not because there aren't buyers, but because the listing process is too manual to make sense. With AI, this is finally changing.

SellRaze turns a photo into a live listing **in seconds.**

Point your camera at anything. Our AI identifies the item, determines what it's actually worth, selects the best photos, fills in every detail, and lists it across multiple marketplaces, automatically. Once it sells, we arrange free pickup from your door.

The entire process, which used to take 30+ minutes, now takes seconds.

launches.body:
**TL;DR:** 

Light Anchor (YC P26) builds fully autonomous e-commerce brands that run at the speed of compute. Consumer brands have always been limited by the speed of humans: hiring, coordinating, and sleeping. AI agents that now run operations end-to-end break all those constraints, making a new kind of consumer business possible: one capped by compute, not headcount.

Today, Light Anchor operates one flagship brand and multiple experiment stores, all run by AI agents on a shared platform that compounds with every new brand launched. The vision is thousands of consumer businesses, operating with little to no human intervention.

<https://youtu.be/_uN-A-4uugA>

### **Why we're doing this**

E-commerce brands have always been bottlenecked by how fast humans can run them. With agents that operate end-to-end, that bottleneck disappears, and a different kind of consumer business becomes possible: one where the cost and speed of operating it isn't capped by headcount.

To test whether agents could do the actual work humans do at an e-commerce brand, we deployed our first agent on Upwork, where small businesses post tasks for freelancers. We started small, with discrete tasks: catalog cleanup, SKU uploads, and data migrations. Within days, our agent had completed 50+ Shopify jobs end-to-end at a 4.9/5 rating, and the same clients started asking for more. "Clean up our catalog" turned into "run our marketing," then "handle our sourcing," then "run the whole storefront." Within 3 weeks, we were running multiple stores end-to-end for owners who used to do this work themselves.

Today we own and operate multiple stores of our own.

### **The agents, platform, and data**

Here are the agents that run our stores:

* **CEO agent**: sets weekly priorities, manages a $10K budget per brand, escalates decisions for human review
* **GM agent**: P&L, merchandising, inventory, sourcing, customer support
* **Marketing agent** ([cherylkim.me](http://cherylkim.me)): creatives and influencer marketing
* **Engineering agent**: unblocks technical work, ships tools

Every brand runs on the same architecture, with a shared layer (agent tooling, integrations, analytics) and a brand-specific layer (memory, policies, and decisions). Both compound: every brand we launch makes the platform smarter, and the marginal cost of launching the next brand keeps falling. Our bet isn't just to operate more stores; it's to understand customers better than any human team can and capture demand the moment it shifts.

Each brand generates a stream of operating decisions (creatives tested, ads spent, suppliers negotiated, tickets closed) that gets written to a central record the agents can read back from.

Humans don’t operate this way because the cost of writing everything down and coordinating across teams is higher than the value. When the operators are agents, that cost goes to zero. Once the record accumulates, a few things become possible: better targeting, faster store setup, and market/consumer simulations.

### **Asks**

launches.tagline: AI agents that sell every visitor on e-commerce sites — and represent the brand to every other agent.
launches.body:
# \*\*\*\*

**TL;DR:** **Kinect builds storefronts that sell, not just show. Our AI agents know each ecommerce brand's catalog, voice, and customer taste — they sell to every visitor on the site, and represent the brand to every external agent (ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity) asking about it from outside.**

**The problem.** For 25 years, the ecommerce storefront has been a static grid with a search bar. Conversion has hovered at 1–3%. Most visitors leave because the surface is passive - it shows them everything, asks them nothing, and expects them to do the work of figuring out what they want.

At the same time, brands need to cater to how AI talks and represents their brand when conversations are held off platform. ChatGPT shopping queries doubled in six months. As more shoppers ask agents to compare and decide before they ever land on a brand, brands are losing control of how they're described — what those agents say about a brand is whatever they guessed from a public catalog scrape, not what the brand would want them to say.

**What we built.** On the brand's site, Kinect's agents sell every visitor — running sales conversations like concierge, adapting and personalizing product pages to customer segments in real-time, picking the right recommendation for the question being asked. The agent picks up on what each shopper actually wants by looking at where they came from, what they are doing on site, their searches, filters, order history, and more. The storefront stops being a static grid and starts being a salesperson.

Off-site, we expose an enriched brand-owned data layer makes the brand legible to ChatGPT, Gemini, and Perplexity. Structured catalog, brand voice, fit notes, return reasons, segment-level nuance — all exposed in formats external agents can actually use. When an agent describes the brand, the version it describes is now the one the brand would want them to. All of this sits on a parallel Agent storefront that is context rich, structured, and catered specifically for agents to read and scrape. The Kinect agents are also available for the agents to talk too, ask questions, and more.

**One brand layer built for all surfaces.** Built for scaling DTC e-commerce brands.

**Launch Video: [https://youtu.be/fSOVQKz8AVM](https://youtu.be/fSOVQKz8AVM)**

**Early Traction**

* 11 customers live across Wellness, Fashion, Sporting Goods, and Consumer Goods
* Engaged users with our sales agents convert 2.4x higher
* 80% of conversations are first time customers unfamiliar with brands
* 10-15% conversion gains for early beta partners

**Backstory**

Kratik and I spent the past year at Reevo building conversational intelligence for B2B sales – extracting buyer intent from dialogue, helping enterprise teams understand what prospects actually wanted, and close more deals faster. We also used AI to scrape and research customers and know where the gaps are in discovery.

As we built for B2B reps, our E-Commerce friends kept asking for something like this for their own brands – a way to reimagine the website to drive conversion and personalization. So we got to work.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=100032&key=user_uploads/3413616/85f4ba2e-bbaa-4b31-86ef-557f1a764b63)

If you know someone who runs an E-Commerce brand (or you are one) – we’d like to give them early access + dinner on us for you! We're looking for:

* Founders, marketing, and E-Commerce leaders at D2C brands

Reach out on Bookface or [kratik@trykinect.ai](https://kratik@trykinect.ai) + [varun@trykinect.ai](https://varun@trykinect.ai)

launches.tagline: Why can't e-commerce companies scale like tech companies?
launches.body:
tl;dr: Why can't e-commerce companies scale like tech companies? And how we might be able to change that.

We spent 12 months embedded in the operations of 30 e-commerce brands\! Here’s what we learnt:

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=107204&key=user_uploads/3288698/1a3cc8c3-db71-4d81-b2ad-9679b77f9451)

**What we saw:** Each company had a unique operational setup with a mix of 5 to 7 tools glued together to run the shop. To keep all these tools running smoothly with each other, it requires a lot of tedious admin. As a result, headcount increases as the company scales.

Most companies couldn't even automate a basic return processing, let alone offer exchanging items or build an AI agent to approve returns or send shipping label to the customer.

Expansion made it worse: more countries and/or SKUs = exponentially more problems.

**What we built:** We have built an agentic OS for e-commerce: You connect your shop stack, then describe how you want to handle shipments, returns, refunds, or claims → Pango builds the return portal, fixes the delivery options, and builds a customer service process and agent for you.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=107204&key=user_uploads/3288698/ceed8a01-52aa-403a-9986-758da64ff4e4)

**Result:** So far we have managed to automate 99% of returns and shipping operations, reduce operation costs by 20% and sign 30 global brands.

launches.body:
**Palisade builds agents to run your online marketplace. Our agents have driven over $2.7M in GMV since the start of the batch.**

<https://youtu.be/cuVQHgQ9yHg>

**The problem:** The best marketplaces in the real world run on salespeople. The real estate agent who takes you house to house and texts you the moment the right listing is about to hit the market. The Sephora beauty advisor who finds your exact shade. The jeweler who walks you through diamond cuts for an engagement ring. **Online marketplaces skipped that person entirely** and left the selling to search bars and filters.

**What we do:** Palisade builds the missing **sales agent**. Every single visitor to your marketplace gets their own dedicated agent, and conversion goes up massively.

**How it works:** Agents can take any action possible on your platform. They know every listing, every UI component, and every flow. They navigate for users with their own cursor, help them discover, add to cart, and complete the purchase or booking. They build custom pages and reshape the UI around how each person actually uses the platform, remembering each user and tailoring the experience to their behavior and preferences. Each dedicated agent can naturally text and email with their customer as well.

**Is this another chatbot?** Each agent is proactive with much richer, customized components than an idle chatbot. It’s like giving every customer an omnipotent Claude embedded into the platform. Palisade agents get to know each customer personally and build relationships over time. They keep working after customers leave, remember them when they return, and reach out proactively over email and text with personal messages. And everything they learn flows back: agents aggregate their conversations into reports, insights, and recommendations for sellers, and offer to make concrete optimizations themselves, to the listings and even to the marketplace platform itself.

**Integration**: Start by adding just one line of code to your existing platform, whether your marketplace sells yachts, vacation rentals, rare collectibles, or anything else.

**Backstory:** After studying CS at Princeton, I spent years at Amazon building software for influencers to sell more products. I then became a founding engineer at Sage AI Labs, where I worked on some of the very first iMessage agents for consumer shopping. That work left me with a deep understanding of consumer habits and marketplace dynamics.

**If you’re looking to transform your marketplace:** Reach out at [jonathan@runpalisade.com](mailto:jonathan@runpalisade.com)
